prose.summary: Illustrators create original imagery that communicates a story, concept or product need. The role differs from graphic design because the core deliverable is image-making, while graphic designers organize type, image and layout into a broader communication system.
prose.day_to_day: The work moves from brief and references to sketches, feedback, finished artwork and production files. Illustrators adapt style, composition and detail to the audience and medium rather than drawing only what interests them. Revision may involve both the image and the underlying concept. File preparation, licensing terms and clear handoff matter alongside visual quality.
prose.work_environment: This is largely studio or laptop-based work, and the measured openings showed meaningful remote availability. Client meetings and collaboration can be remote, while some production contexts require local access. Workload can be uneven when assignments are project-based or revisions arrive close to delivery.
prose.getting_in: Build a portfolio for a market, not a general archive of personal art. The measured skills emphasize illustration and Photoshop, with motion, writing, the Illustrator application, Unreal, Blender and three-dimensional modeling also present. Show briefs, exploratory work, final images and production-ready files. The detailed sample showed no education gate, so the portfolio carries most of the proof.
prose.ladder: Early illustrators execute defined assignments and build consistency. Later they handle larger campaigns, art direction, client relationships or a recognized specialty. The path can branch toward graphic design, brand, motion, games, visualization or technical art.
prose.suits: This work suits people who want image-making to serve a brief and can revise without treating feedback as ownership theft. It is a poor fit if you need predictable project flow, dislike business development or only want to repeat one personal subject. Consistency and file discipline matter as much as isolated standout images.
prose.misconceptions: An illustrator is not simply someone who draws well. The professional task is to solve a communication brief in a style, format and schedule another person can use.
prose.who_qualifies: Graphic and brand designers bring communication context, while game designers and technical artists may bring production and engine knowledge. Motion designers can extend still image skills over time. Each route needs a portfolio where original imagery, not layout or code, is clearly the applicant's contribution.
prose.what_the_numbers_miss: Listings cannot show how much of an illustrator's workload comes from finding clients, negotiating scope and chasing approvals. That unpaid operating work changes the economics of independent practice.

steps.how: Select editorial, publishing, advertising, games or another context so the portfolio answers a recognizable kind of brief.
Create several images with consistent visual logic while varying subject, composition and format enough to show range.
Include selected sketches, the communication problem and a revision decision so reviewers can judge process, not only finish.
Deliver the requested dimensions, layers, color handling and naming, then make scope and usage terms clear before starting client work.

prose.tools: Illustration and Photoshop lead the measured skills. Motion design, the Illustrator application, Unreal, Blender and three-dimensional modeling show distinct production branches. Use tools that fit the target market and keep the portfolio centered on the images and decisions they support.

faq.q: illustrator vs graphic designer, what is the difference?
faq.a: An illustrator creates original imagery, while a graphic designer organizes type, image and layout around a communication system. Many projects use both skills.
